newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Tuesday with investors pulling out money to prepare for a new share issue on Wednesday, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 12.52 percent from 11.86 percent on Monday.
Turnover fell to 8.47 million lots from 10.52 million Monday. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the share issue of Xiamen International Trading (Group) Co, a domestic A share firm, pushed up early-maturing contracts in particular today.
Traders expect the rates to move in a narrow box tomorrow with the listing of a new A share firm, Jiangsu Sopo Co.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on weak sentiment despite a technical rebound last Friday, traders said. The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 120.58 yuan from 120.68 yuan.
Combined volume on the eight-contract market fell to 1.16 million lots from 1.45 million.
Traders said technical charts indicated that prices would stabilise after losses in the previous two weeks with the 10-year bond likely to find support at the 120.00 yuan level.
